# Errors — neode v1.0.0-next.1

> unrelated OGMs. Regenerate with `pnpm docs:agents`.

Typed error taxonomy and driver-error classification. House rule (NTS-442): every error names what failed, where, why, and suggests the fix — `<what failed> in <where> — <why>. <suggested fix>`, with did-you-mean suggestions for near-miss keys. Driver failures carry the failing statement with REDACTED parameters (keys and shapes, never values); ValidationError lists every failing property, not just the first.

### `CardinalityViolationError` (class)

Raised when a write would give a relationship more edges than its declared cardinality allows (NTS-161): relating a second edge onto a `one` / `zeroOrOne` relationship — through relate(), a multi-target save, or syncEdges — names the relationship, the violated cardinality and the fix. Detach the existing edge first (or use syncEdges, which detaches for you), or change the declaration to `many`.

_source: errors/cardinality-violation.ts_

### `classifyError` (function)

Map a raw driver/engine error to the typed taxonomy (NTS-129): constraint violations → ConstraintViolationError, transient codes and retryable-flagged failures → TransientError. Everything else — unknown shapes and already-typed errors — passes through untouched.

_source: errors/classify.ts_

### `ConstraintViolationError` (class)

A unique-constraint violation, raised on `merge()`/`create()` flows that race an existing node. `label`/`property` are parsed from the database message when it names them (Neo4j does; the embedded Relate engine only names the constraint), and stay undefined otherwise.

_source: errors/constraint-violation.ts_

### `isTransientError` (function)

Type guard for classified transient errors.

_source: errors/classify.ts_

### `NeodeError` (class)

Base class of the typed error taxonomy (NTS-129). Typed errors are produced by `classifyError`, which wraps the raw driver/engine error — the original is preserved as `cause`. House rule (NTS-442): every error names what failed, where, why, and suggests the fix — `<what failed> in <where> — <why>. <suggested fix>`. Driver failures carry the failing statement with REDACTED parameters (`redactParameters` — keys and shapes, never values).

_source: errors/neode-error.ts_

### `OptimisticLockError` (class)

Raised when an optimistic-lock check (NTS-158) matched zero rows: the `@Version` property the instance was hydrated with no longer matches the stored one — the node was modified or deleted by another transaction. This is NOT a transient failure: retrying without reloading will fail again. Reload the entity (find / findById / a fresh get) and re-apply the change. The stable `name` lets retry helpers exclude it from transient- retry classification.

_source: errors/optimistic-lock.ts_

### `RelationNotLoadedError` (class)

Raised when strict relation access is on (setStrictRelationAccess) and a relationship property the load spec did not request is read off a hydrated entity (NTS-155). The message names the exact fix: request the relation in the load spec (`with`) or load it on the instance.

_source: errors/relation-not-loaded.ts_

### `TransientError` (class)

A transient failure (`Neo.TransientError.*` codes, or the driver's / engine's own `retryable` verdict): retrying the operation may succeed. `isRetryable` is baked in by the code classification — a TransientError is only ever created for a retryable failure.

_source: errors/transient.ts_
